ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. where is the library
   B. Where is the library
   C. Where is the Library
   D. Where is the library?

2. When practising Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

3. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. One main idea with supporting sentences
   D. Only one word repeated

4. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

5. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. quickly
   C. run
   D. happiness

6. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. went
   B. goes
   C. goed
   D. going

7. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

8. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

10. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a describing word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only an action

11. When practising Play: Structure and Setting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Play: Structure and Setting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Play: Structure and Setting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Play: Structure and Setting.

12. When practising Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 7.5.1 The Writing Process and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Where is the library?

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Plot.

3. C — One main idea with supporting sentences

4. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Gender Neutral Language.

5. C — run

6. A — went

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Independent Reading - Grade Appropriate Text.

8. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple Poems.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Polite Language.

10. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Play: Structure and Setting.

12. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.5.1 Legibility and Neatness.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 7.2.1 Intensive Reading: Interpretation and Evaluation; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar in Use 7.3.1 Relative Pronouns: Interrogative Pronouns; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 7.4.1 Intensive Reading: Play; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 7.5.1 The Writing Process; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
